reviews.text: Wall World 2 is an awesome sequel that improves everything from the first game. Exploring the endless wall, mining resources, and fighting enemies is super fun and feels really rewarding. The world looks beautiful, the music fits perfectly, and upgrades keep every run exciting. It’s easy to lose track of time — “just one more dive” turns into hours of gameplay.

I've been waiting for this for a while. Simply put, it's bigger, better and all-around an upgrade to WW1 that doesn't actually require you playing it. The player now has a lot more to do, like visiting the city and interacting with the NPCs. I think it's fair to say anyone who enjoyed WW1 would be into this.

Definitely not worth the time. The game is extremely repetitive and even gets boring. I expected it to take around 5 to 10 hours to finish, but it ended up taking way longer than I thought. The game itself has a cool theme, but it becomes excessively repetitive and boring as you spend hours playing it. I completed 100% of the achievements, and the story is actually interesting, but it's very slow since the plot is only revealed little by little over time. The most enjoyable part was really understanding the story and seeing the environment change. But the gameplay is tedious, bad and full of bugs that ruin the experience, and not to mention the runs are extremely boring. There’s no procedural generation in the game, which would’ve made it much more interesting. I do not recommend the game.

I played the first game, it wasn't exactly a masterpiece, but I liked it. I played this one, and while it also has some issues, I'd say it's fine overall. I especially liked how there are so many in-mission upgrade options, so you need to make choices each time: are you going for the leviathan fight or just quick extraction? do you want to invest into mining buffs and maybe make a return on that? The quests to get upgrades were also a nice addition. I feel that a lot of criticism in the recent negative reviews is coming from the players who maybe haven't quite adjusted to the changes, and are trying to play this as if it's the first game. I'll try to address some of their points: > The game discourages you from buying temporary upgrades during the run because same resources are needed for permanent upgrades. Not exactly true: you get dust for the resources you spent during the the run. And the main bottleneck is dust. > The mining phase is very slow You're supposed to use relics and bar buffs to speed up mining. The game offers quite a number of relics that allow you to quickly destroy blocks. If you buff up and give a couple of upgrades to the docking station, you can pretty much clear all blocks even in the latest areas before the time runs out. This makes you play strategically: set aside a bit of money for buffs, hunt relics that help mining, then go bananas with the drill. > The spider guns are unbalanced, and some are worse than the starting weapon. I found all guns interesting to play with when fully upgraded, and certainly more fun than the starting weapon. Having tried all weapons fully upgraded, I can confidently say that no gun is worse than the starting gun (you might not be able to beat Levi with the shotgun, but that's about it.) > We need to repeat missions just to get upgrades This one depends on one's playstyle I think. I spent a lot of time in each mission, and I was running of things to spend my resources on, being only blocked from progression by needing gems from next zone to buy new stuff.

I was a big fan of the first Wall World. Despite some flaws, my main criticism was that it felt too short, I really wanted to spend longer in this world. So I was really excited for this sequel, since it meant more of what I liked. However, it feels like the devs overcorrected a lot. The game abandons the massive level you can spend hours climbing, and instead has a "missions" system, where you choose a mission to go on, complete it, and go back to a hub. This *does* make the game longer. It also makes it very grindy. The appeal of Wall World to me was... the Wall. This infinite stretch of rock that you can climb in either direction, exploring and gathering resources while repellling waves of enemies. That was the Wall World fantasy. I am baffled by this decision to remove the "infinite" nature of the Wall. Instead of feeling like an explorer, bravely climbing where no one has gone before, you repeat the same missions in the same environments, complete the research bar, do one special mission, then rince and repeat. And those missions aren't varied or interesting enough to keep me engaged, either. That's not to say everything is bad in WW2. There's a lot of improvements in several areas. QoL, upgrades, world building, combat, a lot changed for the better. I especially like the new combat in the mines, which feels engaging and breaks the monotony of mining. I love love love the bigger mines, there's such a visceral pleasure to digging deeper and deeper and having to make a mental map of where you are and keeping track of what you've already explored, where the dangers are, where the loot is, etc. But... here comes the second incomprehensible decision. One of the best gameplay loops of WW was the push and pull of going further in the mine for just a little more loot vs the threat of the Zygex raids. If you didn't plan your trips carefully, you could lose precious seconds at the start of the next raid, and that pressure was integral to the game. This is why I cannot understand the reasoning behind adding teleporters in the mine. These blocks, that you can find easily and often, straight-up just teleport you immediately at the mine entrance without any drawbacks, as many times as you want, thus negating any sense of danger and tension. Why be careful not to go too far in the mine? Why worry about inventory space? Why bother memorizing the mine layout? Just find a teleporter and bam, you're home free with time to spare for the raid. All of the risk and reward, the tension, the thrill of exploring deeper, gone. If the teleporters where one-time use, or harder to find, or required a resource to activate, maybe they could have been fine, but as they are they kinda ruin the experience. This, plus the mission structure, makes Wall World 2 a lot less fun than the first game, and that's such a shame. I wanted the combat to be a lot more like Risk of Rain, where the danger keeps ramping up and up and up, and you need to move your ass if you want to keep up with the enemies. I wanted the mining to be more like Minecraft, where you get lost in the caves and need to find your way back. I wanted the world to feel more like Rogue Legacy, where you keep going foward and go a little further each run. I wanted the lore to be more like Axiom Verge, full of questions and mysteries, but with enough information to piece it together yourself (why is there no menu to read the lore you've found?) This is my biggest problem with Wall World 2 : I wanted it to be a lot more than it actually is. I wanted the team at Alawar to identify the strengths of their game, and hone in on the fun at the core of it. Instead it feels like they took every step to move away from it, which baffles me. Anyway, if like me you wanted more Wall World, well there is some of it in here. I can't deny that I had some fun playing the game. I'm finding it difficult to recommand playing Wall World 2, but a lot of it comes from how thouroghly the game disappointed me. It's not a bad game, just not the game I wanted.

Should've been a DLC. Added a few weapons? So many just copied from the first game. But you can no longer get more than one per mission. 50% or more of the weapons/relics are trash, not even worth picking up. If you could remove a relic/weapon from the rotation it'd be great, using the meta currency or something. There are some very questionable design decisions. For instance, all the buildings at the mine entrance are copied over from the first game, no changes. These turrets that stay at one spot on the wall, is useless when you're moving up and down the wall to get the resources and do tasks. The drinks at the bar: an interesting addition that the first game didn't have, but there's only one, maybe two correct drink combinations. Mining speed, backpack size, % chance of materials. All others are useless: Damage to Zyrex, Defense from Zyrex, health in the mine, idfk I didn't even look very closely at them. I never once had a problem with Zyrex in the mine. The first weapon will do just fine, upgraded fully. Finally, the final boss. turns into a bullet heck, (kinda) as it was very easy to dodge everything. Very unlike the rest of the game. Also surprisingly buggy, but nothing game breaking.

Honestly, if you're coming from the first Wall World you should hold your expectations as this is a similar game yet almost a different genre, a lot of the fun jank is gone, the mining doesn't have the same charm to it, there are enemies in the mines and spawners designed to slow your progression by hindering you when alive or forcing waves when killed and the individual missions feel too short to be considered roguelike. If you're looking for less of a roguelike and something with a lot more story depth you will enjoy this, there is significantly more meta progression and a world to explore with different missions that you extract from after completing the objectives. For me wall world 2 is what darkest dungeon 2 was to darkest dungeon, while I didn't hate the few hours I played of it I do not see myself picking this up again.

终于是全成就通关了，先说结论：完全不推荐购买！！！（steam吞了写了1h的评论我也要再写一遍！！！！） 不知道这一代为什么要把那个矿整的屎一样难挖，点三级矿力才跟一代点一级一样，局外成长更是屁用没有，很难想象开着CE都玩的如此难受，每开一个任务都跟新下载游戏一样，最操蛋是我都点满挖掘了，依旧挖不动，还得把分钻头点满才行，本来前期就坐牢，这下每把都是牢中牢。前作后期得益于蜘蛛增益+炸弹,基本直接跳过发育，这一带tm炸弹改鞭炮了，重力挖掘服、蜘蛛增益、脉冲枪全删了md，一代为了爽脉冲枪我真的打完还开了几把1h的局，这一代能通关都是我已经非常耐心了。 第二就是这代流程真的有大问题，完全就是为了任务而任务，非任务矿洞一点意义都没有（除非要打BOSS），炸一下吃点资源都已经是非常给面子了，大部分时候我都是直奔任务点，顶着三级挖矿，完成任务就跑，一秒不想多待，完全没有意义。而且这代矿洞设计有个非常蛋疼的点是，很多大任务矿洞都是U形的设计，众所周知这游戏任务点都是右上角，强制绕路我还能接受，但是有些超大矿洞又tm黑又tm绕，对路痴非常不友好，有几次打完守点任务迷路死掉我真的想卸载了。 第三就是战斗更是给这坨大粪上点缀了满满的一波苍蝇，打怪有惩罚，跨区域有惩罚，有时候前期初始区域资源没那么多，又要点挖掘又要点武器，这个时候强迫你跨区域甚至能直接被一波打掉2/3血，有时候打完一波下矿进去打几个巢穴又tm怪潮了，太恶心了，还经常几个巢穴长一起。而且这一作怪的伤害大幅提升，护盾直接变成超薄了，摸一下就碎甲，那个从天上掉下来挡路是最tm sb的，碰撞体积贼大，碰两下腿毛就碎甲。而且前期摸到抛物线武器你就用吧，谁不想急头白脸的在怪潮来的时候疯狂马枪。 骂完了爽快了，不过ww2还是有要夸的地方，首先就是这一作对剧情有极大的补充与发展，非常的有意思，如果好好写的话潜力巨大，遗憾的是如果你想玩WW3那么2还是得买。而且这作体量非常大，地图、武器、方块有非常新东西（增加矿洞内回城点好评）终于有点成熟游戏框架的味道了，只不过又臭又长hhhh。说到最后，最最最最最值得夸奖的还是还是蜘蛛那几套装备，吞噬者套装帅爆了好吗，只能说好好做吧，我真的很爱挖矿，出了ww3我大概率还是会买的，求求你了让大伙挖个爽吧！！！！

Surprised how good it is, given the mostly positive review score. It got backlash for not innovating enough, and also because instead of just being designed to be a roguelike, you have campaign missions which you complete and unlock. Having been a few years since I played the first Wall World, I don't notice how much of it was borrowed from the first game, but there's definitely new stuff in it - so that criticism isn't an issue for me. The second criticism comes down to personal preferences - The mission structure. This is something I really like about the game, adding an extra bit of progression to compel me to keep playing. If anything this might be my favourite 2D miner, but kind of a toss up between both Wall Worlds and Dome Keeper. The game has a neat soundtrack too. I think Insane mode is probably the best way to play it, as the difficulty really drops off on hard mode (what I spent most of my time playing it on). Pity that wasn't the default. You can change the difficulty whenever and there's unfortunately no achievements tied to difficulties. So yeah, neat game!

At first, more Wall World sounded pretty great. New environments, a more robust story, more combat and obstacles in caves. There are even more types of leviathans and robo-spider parts, pretty sweet! Unfortunately, the game runs way too long if you want to actually finish all side missions, even though half of them aren't even necessary to unlock everything. Progression could have used some more fine tuning, because by the time I unlocked all the best stuff I still had about 10 hours of playtime left on the missions. The first game was short, sweet and memorable. This one is more ambitious, and if you want more Wall World, definitely give it a shot, but it lost something from its simplicity and charm.

I loved Wall World, and I want to love Wall World 2 so badly But it just barely falls short of being a sequel, alone it's fine, but as a sequel to Wall World? Meh. It feels like they wanted to use Wall World as a base, which makes sense of course, but they just ended up recycling far to much and overall it means that a lot of stuff just feels Copy/Pasted from the original game And the aspects that they did try to change or add onto just don't quite hit the spot, like they either didn't change enough or the changes just don't feel great Stuff like the extraction mechanic just... don't really feel good? I don't really like it at all honestly. And there really just aren't enough Meta Upgrades too! Or rather, it feels like a lot of the Meta Upgrades are in the wrong spot. The leg and hulls are neat, but there could be a few more of them. And I really wish you could upgrade more of your mining tool, so that the beginning or every mission didn't just feel like this massive drag. That and I think the biggest thing that I wanted from this sequel that wasn't done, I highly dislike the fact that you can't unlock more weapons permanently, sure you can unlock more weapons for in the mines, but I'd really wish they'd allow you to unlock at least 2-3 other weapons you can start with and upgrade. I loved the first *Wall World* and earned 100% of its achievements, so I was very excited to see the concept expanded in a sequel. This is one of my favorite styles of game: mining for resources, working through upgrade trees, exploring dangerous areas, fighting enemies directly, and periodically defending yourself against waves of monsters. The first game blended all of those elements extremely well, and *Wall World 2* gives me more of what I enjoyed while expanding the world, its lore, and the number of technologies and upgrades available. Some players may complain that it is too similar to the first game, but I completely disagree. I **loved** the first one. I did not want the sequel to abandon what made it work; I wanted it to build on that foundation, and that is exactly what this game does. One change irritated me at first. Many of the improvements purchased during an expedition are lost when the mission ends. I may be remembering the first game incorrectly since I played it about two years ago, but progression initially felt less permanent here. After sticking with it, however, I found that I did not mind nearly as much as I expected. There are still plenty of permanent upgrades to unlock when you return to town, while the temporary upgrades give each mission its own progression and rhythm. I also really like the new structure of traveling to different areas of the overworld and taking on specific missions. It makes the world feel larger and gives each expedition more of a purpose. The setting remains one of the strongest parts of the series. An entire civilization lives on the side of an apparently endless wall, with no surviving memory or history of anything beyond it and no knowledge of whether the wall even has a top or bottom. That is a fascinating concept. The Lovecraftian monsters may not be completely original, but cosmic horror is a trope I never get tired of. The game captures that unsettling feeling that humanity is like a colony of ants, barely capable of understanding how enormous, ancient, and strange the world outside our experience really is. If you enjoyed the first *Wall World*, this is an easy recommendation. It keeps the satisfying gameplay loop that made the original so addictive while giving us more to discover, more ways to improve, and more mysteries surrounding this wonderfully strange world.

If you played the first game, this will be...more of the first game. But I have to say, it's not as good. For one, they did away with the simple 'trying to get to the top of the wall' premise, where each run was that singular goal with randomly generated caves. Instead, you now do a bunch of missions with specific objectives. The formula is largely the same, but the little differences start to add up, and not in a good way. They added enemies to the mines, which seems like a good change, but they're so inconsequential it makes no real difference. They're borderline not even enemies, just obstacles that take extra time to deal with. However, because they've added combat inside the mine, they ALSO added a bunch of powerups and augments for that combat...which as I indicated are wholly unnecessary since the combat is so easy. So you end up picking up a bunch of powerups that are basically useless, cluttering your upgrade menu with a bunch of things you'll never use. It got to the point that, instead of being excited when I saw one of the powerup balls, I actually started feeling annoyance, because there was a 50/50 chance of it being some useless ability for mine combat that I didn't want. Overall I think this is a step down from the first game. The spider controls are better, and that's just about all I can say about it. Otherwise I'd just recommend playing the first one.
